name: Ready position
summary: The stance you start every point in and come back to after every shot.
whenToUse: Always. Between every shot you return here, so the next ball never catches you upright or off balance.

keyPoints.stance: Feet a little wider than your shoulders. Right-handers: right foot slightly back (left-handers: left foot back).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Knees bent, lean forward from the hips, weight on the balls of your feet so your heels are light.
keyPoints.strokeLength: No stroke here. This is the base every stroke starts from and ends in.
keyPoints.timing: Be set just as your opponent hits the ball. A tiny hop or settle at that moment helps you push off either way.
keyPoints.tablePosition: About an arm's length plus a little behind the end line, slightly toward your backhand corner.
keyPoints.freeArm: Up and in front of you, relaxed, roughly mirroring your bat arm.
keyPoints.batArm: Bat in front of your body at about table height, elbow relaxed and slightly away from your side.
keyPoints.recovery: After each shot, bring the bat back in front and your feet back to this width.
keyPoints.anticipation: Watch your opponent's bat, not just the ball. Their swing tells you the spin and direction.

cues: Bat in front, at table height

learningPath.task: Watch the 3D player settle into ready from the front and the side. Notice the knee bend and where the bat sits.
learningPath.passCheck: You can name the three cues.

learningPath.task: Copy the player: step into ready, hold for 3 seconds, stand up, repeat. Then add a small side step and come back to ready.
selfChecks: Are your feet wider than your shoulders?
Can you lift your heels without falling backward?
Is your bat in front of you, not at your side?

learningPath.task: Play an easy rally and come back to ready after every single hit, even the easy ones.
learningPath.passCheck: You return to ready after 10 hits in a row.

learningPath.task: Footwork with ready in between: two-point side steps, landing in ready each time.
learningPath.passCheck: A full set without standing up straight.

learningPath.task: Push then drive. The change of stroke is where people forget ready, so make it a habit there.
learningPath.passCheck: 7 of 10 patterns with a clear return to ready.

learningPath.task: Play points and check yourself after each one: did you get back to ready before their shot?
learningPath.passCheck: Ready in time for most balls in a game to 11.

learningPath.task: Test: two-point footwork for 60 seconds, landing in ready each time.
learningPath.passCheck: 30 clean shots in 60 seconds, or 4 rounds of shadow steps staying low.

gamePatterns.how: Step back into ready straight away. Most missed third balls start with standing still after serving.
Push off your outside foot and come back toward the middle in ready, because the next ball often goes to the other corner.

troubleshooting.symptom: I feel slow to the ball
causes: Not resetting after your last shot
fixes: Lean forward until your heels feel light
Bend your knees a little more
Say 'back' to yourself after every hit

troubleshooting.symptom: I'm off balance when I hit
fixes: Move your feet first, then swing

causes: Bat drops to your side between shots
Watching only the ball, not the opponent
fixes: Keep the bat in front at table height
Watch their bat to read the ball earlier

penholdNotes: The same stance. Many penholders stand a bit more toward the backhand corner to cover more balls with the forehand.
